name: NGINX
baseline: Apache httpd (Apache2, version and MPM not stated on the benchmark page)
workload: wrk with 12 threads and 500 connections for 5 s against the same static page on localhost (no file name or size given); requests/sec and latency for NGINX default config, NGINX tuned config (denji/nginx-tuning) and Apache2; best of three runs.
claimed_speedup: Requests/sec: NGINX Default 116415.16 vs Apache2 62124.60, about 1.9x (derived from page data); NGINX Tuned 201407.17 vs Apache2 62124.60, about 3.2x (derived from page data). Average latency: NGINX Default 4.24 ms and Tuned 2.40 ms vs Apache2 178.92 ms. Cross-check in a second third-party run (ApacheBench in Docker, nginx 1.11.8 vs Apache 2.4.25 event MPM, concurrency 50): 20166.17 vs 16951.31 req/s with keep-alive (+19%), 5454.22 vs 4827.32 req/s without (+13%).
compiler_and_flags: Not stated (no build flags; nginx and Apache versions and configs not given on the page; load command: wrk -c 500 -t 12 -d 5s http://127.0.0.1:8081/ for NGINX, wrk -c 500 -t 12 -d 5 http://127.0.0.1:80/ for Apache2)
hardware: Intel Core i7-8550U at 1.80 GHz, 8 CPUs, about 25.1 GB RAM, Linux kernel 5.17.5 x86_64
tradeoffs: Event-driven master/worker design with a small, mostly flat per-connection memory footprint, so it suits many idle or slow connections; dynamic content goes through proxy/FastCGI/uwsgi upstreams rather than in-process modules like mod_php. No per-directory .htaccess override, so configuration is central and needs a reload. Most third-party modules must be compiled in or built as dynamic modules against the same nginx version and flags. Written in C, so memory-safety bugs are possible.
caveats: No first-party benchmark in the nginx repository: its README has no performance content and does not mention Apache. The numbers come from the README-linked BENCHMARKS.md of binserve (a competing Rust static server, MIT), which publishes the NGINX and Apache2 rows only as reference baselines for its own results. Tier C: CPU, OS and wrk flags are stated, but nginx and Apache versions, config files, served file, MPM and compiler flags are not given, so it is not reproducible. Apache2 ran on port 80 and NGINX on 8081 (possibly an untuned distro Apache against a tuned nginx), and Apache2 average latency of 178.92 ms with stdev 244 ms at 500 connections suggests a worker or connection limit rather than raw speed; the 5 s runs are short and take the best of three. The tuned NGINX row uses an outside tuning guide. The cross-check at https://gist.github.com/lukassup/d5ad12753ee13325b177429db01e0258 (nginx 1.11.8 vs Apache 2.4.25, both default welcome pages in Docker with docker-proxy in the path, no CPU stated) is dated and its nginx page is larger than the httpd page (612 B vs 45 B), httpd had 189 failed requests (length mismatches) and the author warns the page sizes may skew results; the gap there is only 13-19%. The listed lead in the book (Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed., ch. 4) calls NGINX an HTTP accelerator / cache, with no numbers. Search snippets (not opened pages) point to other 2026 blog comparisons with nginx ahead on static files at high concurrency, but those hosts were unreachable.
